entries.proposition: Five patients started everolimus before 2 years of age; two had at least 50 percent seizure reduction, one at least 30 percent, one no change and one an increase in seizure frequency.
entries.snippet: Five patients started treatment before 2 years of age. Of these, ≥ 50% reduction in seizure frequency occurred in two patients, and ≥ 30%, no change, and increase in seizure frequency in one each of the other three patients.

entries.proposition: Sixty-one of 64 patients (95 percent) reported clinical adverse effects.
entries.snippet: Sixty-one of the 64 (95%) patients reported clinical adverse effects after follow-up periods

entries.proposition: Adverse effects of grade 3 or higher occurred in 36 percent of patients over the whole period; pneumonia was the most frequent, in 13 percent.
entries.snippet: Adverse effects ≥ grade 3 occurred in 36% of the patients during the entire treatment period. The most frequent adverse effect ≥ grade 3 was pneumonia, which occurred in 13% of the patients.

entries.proposition: The Discussion prints the grade 3 or higher figure as 35 percent.
entries.snippet: Adverse effects ≥ grade 3 were reported in 35% of the patients, and were quite similar to those of EXIST-1 and 3

entries.proposition: Patients with grade 3 or higher adverse effects were younger (median 12 against 23 years, p 0.02).
entries.snippet: Patients with adverse effects ≥ grade 3 were younger than patients without adverse effects ≥ grade 3 during the entire treatment period (p: 0.02, Md: 12 vs. 23 years)

entries.proposition: Half of patients required dose modifications due to adverse effects.
entries.snippet: Fifty percent required dose modifications due to adverse effects.

entries.proposition: Hospitalisation or prolongation of hospitalisation was required in 34 percent of the sample.
entries.snippet: Hospitalisation or prolongation of hospitalisation was required in 34% of the sample

entries.proposition: Nine patients (14 percent) discontinued; four for adverse effects, one of them cerebral oedema.
entries.snippet: Nine patients (14%) discontinued treatment; four due to adverse effects (leukopenia, neutropenia and COVID-19 infection, cerebral oedema, oral ulceration)

entries.proposition: The Results print a median treatment duration of 15 months (range 0 to 28, mean 13, SD 7.9, 95 percent CI 6.9 to 19.1).
entries.snippet: The median duration of treatment was 15 months (range 0–28, mean 13, SD: 7.9, 95% CI 6.9–19.1).

entries.proposition: The patient-characteristics table prints median months of follow-up of 31 (range 0 to 106) for all indications.
The authors note that other anti-seizure medications were changed in most patients and some had surgery, so the cause of seizure change is hard to attribute.
entries.snippet: Other ASMs were changed in a majority of the patients, and some underwent epilepsy surgery, which made it difficult to draw conclusions on the cause of the change in seizure frequency.

entries.proposition: One patient had an immunodeficiency disorder; the authors write that infections increased after treatment initiation, making everolimus a probable cause.
entries.snippet: Clinically infections increased significantly after treatment initiation, making everolimus treatment a probable cause.
